SPECIFICATION FOR 

FEED LIFTING ROCK SHAFT CRANK FOR SEWING 

MACHINES FOR HOUSEHOLD PURPOSES 



1, Scope — Lays down the requirements for feed lifting rock shaft cranks for sewing machines for 
household purposes. 

2. Nomenclature — Shall be as shown in Fig. 1.

3. Material — The feed lifting rock shaft crank shall be made from cast iron conforming to grade 
FG 150 of IS : 210-1978 ' Specification for grey iron castings ( third revision ) '. 

4. Dimensions — Shall be as shewn in Fig. 2.

IS : 10306 - 1982 

5. Tolerances 

5-1 The error in parallelism of the axis of the main holes of the feed lifting rock shaft crank shall be 
within G'15 mm per 100 mm. 

5.2 The error in the squareness of the bearing faces with respect to the main holes shall not 
exceed 0*2 mm per 100 mm. 

6. Workmanship and Finish 

6.1 The main holes of feed lifting rock shaft crank shall be finished to a good finish. 

6.2 The bearing faces of the bosses of feed lifting rock shaft crank shall be machined to a fine finish 
without any line mark. 

6.3 The casting shall be free from defects, such as cracks, flaws or blow holes and shall be chemically 
coloured or suitably plated. 

7. Marking — The feed lifting rock shaft cranks shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark, if required. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — Each feed lifting rock shaft crank shall be given a suitable anti-rust coating or wrapped 
in vapour phase inhibitor paper (commonly known as VPl paper ). The wrapped feed lifting rock shaft 
cranks shall be securely packed in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each packing shall 
bear the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, the type and description of contents. 

9. Sampling 

9.1 Unless otherwise agreed between the supplier and the purchaser, the sampling plan as given in 
Appendix A shall be followed. For further information, reference may be made to IS : 2500 ( Part I )- 
1973 'Sampling inspection tables ■: Part I Inspection by attributes and by count of defects 
( first revision) \ 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 9.1 ) 
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-1. Scale of Sampling 

A-1.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the feed lifting rock shaft cranks of the same type and manufactured 
from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to 
constitute a lot. 

A-1 .2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests ^hali t>e 
carried out for each lot separately. The number of feed lifting rock shaft cranks to be selected at random 
for this purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

A-1 .3 If the feed lifting rock shaft crank are packed individually, in order to ensure the randomness of 
selection, IS : 4905-1968 ' Methods for random sampling ' shall be used. 

A-1. 4 If the feed lifting rock shaft cranks are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons 
( not less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2 ) shall be chosen at random. 
From each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of feed lifting rock shaft cranks shall 
be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of feed lifting rock shaft cranks 
specified in col 2 of Table 1. 

A-2. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 

A-2.1 The feed lifting rock shaft cranks selected according to A-1. 2 and A-1. 3 or A-1 .4 shall be 
examined for dimensions ( see 4 ), tolerances ( see 5 ), and workmanship and finish ( see 6 ). If the 
number of feed lifting rock shaft cranks failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above 
is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table t, the lot shall be 
declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics.

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard has been prepared to unify and rationalize the types and sizes of sewing machines 
components for manufacturing in economic quantities.
